chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Sayrafi, from Bakkar al-Wasiti, from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali, from Humran ibn A'yun, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) concerning knowledge, who said:

It is your hand from you. Muhammad ibn Ali, the compiler of this book, said: This means that knowledge is not other than Him, and it is from His essential attributes, because Allah, the Mighty and High, is a Self that is All-Knowing and All-Seeing. Our intent in describing Him with knowledge is to negate ignorance from Him. And we do not say that knowledge is separate from Him, because if we said that, and then said that Allah has always been Knowing, we would be affirming with Him something eternal that has always existed. Exalted is Allah, the Elevated and Great, from that.
ai.seo_question: What is the nature of God's knowledge in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (AS) defines divine knowledge as 'your hand from you' (or 'your sign from you'), indicating it is an essential attribute inseparable from God's essence. The compiler, Shaykh al-Saduq, clarifies that attributing knowledge to God is to negate ignorance, not to posit a separate eternal entity alongside Him, thereby preserving divine unity (Tawhid) against the risk of multiplicity in the divine attributes.
